articles.title: White House to shift federal research funds to AI, away from colleges
articles.description: The explicit push to fund AI as a primary research instrument, alongside the 2028 quantum computing deployment target and the 10-reactor nuclear buildout by 2030, points to where a meaningful share of a $200 billion annual budget could flow, potentially a tailwind for quantum computing and AI infrastructure names, as well as nuclear and small modular reactor plays. The flip side is a headwind for the university research funding ecosystem, since large institutions that rely heavily on federal grants could see funding become less predictable if money shifts toward individual fellowships and awards. Because this is a redirection of spending priorities rather than new money, and implementation will play out over the rest of the administration's term, the near-term market reaction is likely to be muted and concentrated in AI, quantum, and nuclear-adjacent sectors rather than broad-based. --- The White House wants federal research money following scientists and AI instead of universities, and colleges are bracing for the fallout. Summary: The Trump administration plans to redirect federal research funding toward individual scientists and AI rather than universities, according to the Wall Street Journal (gated) . The directives will shape a roughly $200 billion annual federal research and development budget for the rest of Trump's second term, per the report. The plan prioritizes fellowships and awards for individuals over institutional funding, and could further hurt large universities reliant on federal grants, the Journal said. A proposed OMB rule would give political appointees more influence over grants and align research with administration priorities, according to the report. The administration set goals to deploy a powerful quantum computer by 2028 and have 10 new large nuclear reactors under construction by 2030, per the Journal. Skeptics cited in the report warned that AI models are prone to errors and that overemphasizing the technology could narrow the range of research pursued. The Trump administration plans to accelerate an overhaul of federal research by directing more support toward individual scientists and artificial intelligence rather than universities, the Wall Street Journal reported, in its latest attempt to speed technological discovery in competition with China. According to a new report and memo released Tuesday by the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, individual scientists can help the country move faster to apply AI in scientific research, the newspaper said. The directives from the office will help shape a roughly 200 billion dollar annual federal research and development budget across government agencies for the remainder of President Trump's second term, the Journal reported. The new guidance could further squeeze large universities that rely heavily on federal research funding, according to the report. The administration wants to prioritize programs such as fellowships and awards that support individuals rather than institutions, citing a prestigious National Science Foundation graduate fellowship and a National Institutes of Health award for creative scientists as models it wants emulated, the Journal said. Some universities could also be constrained by a proposed Office of Management and Budget rule that would give political appointees greater influence over grants and align research funding with administration priorities, per the report. Michael Kratsios, director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy, told the Journal that federal research funding has become stagnant, with too much money going to the same institutions in the same way for decades. Kratsios said he met with the leader of an Ivy League university on Tuesday to discuss the new approach and received a positive response, according to the report. The administration has also argued that excessive bureaucracy at both government agencies and universities has held back American research, and under its plan, individual researchers at universities would receive funding directly, reducing the role universities play as intermediaries, the Journal said. Putting AI at the center of scientific research is another core focus, alongside more ambitious national goals such as deploying a powerful quantum computer by 2028 and having ten new large nuclear reactors under construction by 2030 to expand electricity output, according to the report. The administration has also sought to combine the Energy Department's scientific expertise and supercomputing resources through a program called the Genesis Mission, aimed at using AI to tackle research challenges in partnership with the private sector, the Journal said. Kratsios and OMB Director Russ Vought wrote in their memo that agencies should fund research using AI as a genuine new instrument of discovery rather than simply as a tool to support existing methods, per the report. Skeptics cited by the Journal cautioned that AI models remain prone to errors and that overemphasizing the technology could narrow the range of research approaches scientists are able to pursue. This article was written by Eamonn Sheridan at investinglive.com.

articles.title: How a Hisense MiniLED TV can upgrade your living room
articles.description: TVs have come a long way in the last few years. MiniLED sets are slimmer, brighter, boast impressive features and also have the ability to double as monitors for all your gaming needs. If you’re looking for a new TV that can fit in with all the demands of modern life then MiniLED is the way to go. But, not all work in the same way though, so you’ll want one that gives the best performance in a wide range of settings and with a variety of content. Here’s some things to consider when deciding on a new TV that will fit your home. How will the TV cope in brightly lit rooms? Hisense The physical positioning of a TV can be tricky, as you’ll want to avoid strong sources of light from hitting the screen, say from a window, but also want the freedom to place it wherever best suits the size and shape of the room. A washed out screen due to reflections and poor brightness can seriously compromise your enjoyment of shows and movies, that’s why you’ll want a TV that can handle these kind of environments. The Hisense U6SF is a good choice and makes this scenario a whole lot easier thanks to its anti-reflection and glare-free technology. These work to preserve shadow detail and color accuracy all while reducing reflections and surface glare from the sun or other forms of lighting. This means you can fit the TV into your room, rather than arranging the room around the TV, all in the knowledge that it will provide a consistent and clear picture. Another reason you can be confident of excellent visual performance from the Hisense U6SF is its Hi-QLED MiniLED technology. This includes the PowerFocus lens system, which employs single-refraction lenses to guide light accurately to where it needs to be on the screen. Unlike some other MiniLED TVs, this allows the U6SF to precisely focus the brightness and contrast to 160 local dimming zones, which results in deeper blacks, luminous highlights, sharper edges and a more immersive viewing experience. Movies and TVs shows look distinct and balanced, plus any content will be rendered with pin-point precision to make it easy on the eye. A top brightness of 600 nits also gives it the power to deal comfortably with a range of conditions. The Hisense U6SF supports the major HDR formats, such as Dolby Vision IQ and HDR10+ Adaptive which utlilize their intelligent software alongside sensors in the TV to automatically adjust and optimize the images on the screen so that they best suit the surrounding lighting environment. A dedicated Filmmaker Mode also automatically adjusts the setting so you can enjoy movies just as the creators intended. So, whether its following your favourite sports on a bright sunny afternoon or settling down for an evening with a film classic, the picture will remain balanced, colorful and keep the depth that you need to really lose yourself in the entertainment. Hisense How much room will I need for a MiniLED TV? Another important aspect of choosing a new TV is knowing that it will actually fit into your living space. Thankfully, these days this is a little easier, even though the displays have increased in size. A set like the Hisense U6SF boasts a 65-inch panel, but this is housed in a slim-line unibody design that can be placed close to a wall if you want to sit it on a stand, or you can simply attach it to the wall itself. The built-in speaker system supports Dolby Vision and Atmos surround sound, so there’s no need to attach external speakers, plus the technology that powers the display has the aforementioned anti-reflective and glare-free advantages, plus some clever AI enhancements to ensure that content looks good throughout the day and night. How can AI help improve the performances of a MiniLED TV? Hisense While the term AI can be thrown around quite a lot in the consumer electronics space, sometimes it actually does bring some real-world improvements. Hisense loads up the U6SF with several AI enhancements to make it a truly flexible TV. AI Picture automatically tunes the brightness, contrast and saturation so that it suits the surrounding environment. Paired with the AI light sensor, this ensures that you’ll get peak brightness when the sun is shining, while everything is toned down to make the viewing more comfortable in darker situations. An impressive addition is the AI 4K Upscaler, which uses intelligent software to analyze textures and edges in lower resolution visuals and reconstruct the missing details to bring them up to a 4K equivalence. With this clever feature you can now relax and experience classic content as if it was made today. Sports fans will also appreciate the AI Sports mode and its automatic optimization of settings to create vivid images and pumped up sound to make it seem like you’re in the stadium. This works perfectly with the AI Smooth Motion feature so that all the action avoids any blurs, judders or stutters that could spoil the fun. Is the U6SF TV good for playing games? Hisense Another important role that a modern TV has to play is that of a gaming platform. As consoles and PCs have grown in complexity, the graphical demands they place on displays is more challenging than ever. Traditionally, TVs have lacked the high refresh rates that keep the on-screen action smooth and allow gamers to react instantly to anything thrown at them, often at a frenetic pace. This is where the Hisense U6SF adds another string to its bow, as the panel has a dedicated HDR Game Mode which displays a 144Hz variable refresh rate that can keep up with even the most advanced titles. Thanks to its low-latency motion, the graphics keep clear of stutter and screen tear, while remaining crisp and clear. The Hisense U6SF TV makes it easy to sit back on the sofa and play while still being able to read everything clearly or use split-screen for couch-play with a friend. Its Dolby Atmos surround-sound only adds to the experience, with rich and vibrant soundtracks accompanying your exploits. Upgrade your living room with the Hisense U6SF When you buy a new TV there are plenty of things to consider. Will it last? Can it handle all the latest content? Is it future-proof? How will it fit into my home? Thankfully, the Hisense U6SF has all of these areas covered. The picture will look great in any environment thanks to the AI technology and precise local dimming capabilities. Movies, sports and gaming are equally at home, plus your old content will look even better thanks to the AI 4K upscaler. That’s one less decision to worry about. Upgrade to the Hisense U6SF today!
